primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Normal age-related increase in large-artery stiffness
mechanism: Normal aging is associated with progressive stiffening and reduced compliance of large arteries. Earlier return of reflected pressure waves augments systolic pressure, while reduced elastic recoil contributes to a wider pulse pressure and less effective buffering of abrupt hemodynamic changes.
vignette: A healthy older adult is seen for a routine examination. Blood pressure measurements over several visits show a progressively wider pulse pressure with advancing age. There is no evidence of aortic regurgitation, anemia, thyrotoxicosis, or arteriovenous fistula.
lead: Which of the following normal age-related changes most directly explains this finding?
correct: Decreased compliance of large arteries with earlier return of reflected pressure waves during systole
distractors: Increased aortic compliance with greater elastic recoil during diastole
Progressive reduction in systemic vascular resistance caused by loss of arteriolar smooth muscle tone
Marked increase in baroreceptor sensitivity that exaggerates beat-to-beat pressure changes
Increased left-ventricular diastolic compliance caused by reduced myocardial collagen
distractor_notes: Normal aging decreases rather than increases large-artery compliance, reducing elastic buffering of the pulse.
Systemic vascular resistance does not normally fall because of generalized loss of arteriolar tone; age-related vascular stiffening tends to raise systolic pressure.
Baroreceptor sensitivity tends to decline with aging rather than markedly increase.
Aging is associated with myocardial fibrosis and reduced, not increased, ventricular compliance.
key_expl: With aging, large arteries become stiffer and less compliant. Reflected pressure waves return earlier and augment systolic pressure, while reduced elastic recoil lowers the ability of the arterial tree to buffer pulsatile flow. The result is a characteristic widening of pulse pressure in otherwise healthy older adults.
objective: Relate normal aging to reduced large-artery compliance and a wider pulse pressure.
clues: no high-output state or aortic regurgitation
